chunks: And in another hadith, he said:

The testimony of one under suspicion, the adversary, one repelling a liability, a hired worker, a partner, an accused person, or a subordinate is not valid. And the testimony of a wine-drinker is not accepted, nor the testimony of one who plays chess and backgammon, nor the testimony of a gambler.

key_terms.الْخَصْمِ: an adversary or litigant in opposition to another
key_terms.الْمُرِيبِ: a person whose state gives rise to suspicion
key_terms.بِالشِّطْرَنْجِ: with chess, mentioned here as a disqualifying pastime
key_terms.شَارِبِ الْخَمْرِ: one who drinks wine or intoxicants
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony given before an authority

ai.seo_question: Whose testimony is rejected in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out categories of people whose testimony is to be rejected in legal proceedings due to suspicion, conflict of interest, or conduct that undermines reliability and uprightness. It reflects jurisprudential standards for safeguarding justice and the integrity of witness testimony.
